findings.description: The new lazy name-lookup adds two near-identical `git log -1` branches differing only in the format specifier (%an vs %cn), even though `$kind` (author/committer) already encodes which one to use via its first letter. Could collapse to `git log -1 --format="%${kind:0:1}n" "$sha"`, but given this only runs on the rare violation path in a ~15-line script, the explicit if/else is also defensible for readability.

The closing sentence ('The two fields ahead of the address are an abbreviated hash and a literal, neither of which can contain a delimiter.') just restates what's already visible five lines above in the git log --format string (line 30: '%h|author|%ae%n%h|committer|%ce') — an abbreviated hash and a hardcoded 'author'/'committer' literal obviously can't contain a pipe. It adds length without a non-obvious why, running the comment longer than the insight it carries (AGENTS.md Comments: WHY-not-WHAT).
